answer: Each identity's usable standing is released only after a sequential, non-transferable custody period, and the release rate is super-linear in how many identities an operator runs, so a fleet cannot mature faster than one identity at a time. The cost of one more head is paid in full and is never amortised across the fleet. The canyon is the serial tenure, the sparrow the custody window that must elapse, and the walnut the standing released at the end of it; the canyon is personal, the sparrow is not skippable, and the walnut cannot be inherited by a sibling.
